reasons: The cited grant (p0149) is expressly 'revocable' with no standard and names only Customer, with no affiliate/contractor coverage and no notice path to add them — it fails the fallback on two material terms and touches walk-away territory, so 'deviation' is the correct classification.

The redline is directionally correct and actionable: it deletes 'revocable', extends the grant to Affiliates and Subcontractors acting on Customer's behalf, and confines revocation to termination for Customer's uncured material breach, matching the rule's preferred position for subscription-style licences.

The rationale correctly declines to redline transferability because § 14.10 (p0188) already permits assignment to a successor by merger, consolidation or acquisition — avoiding over-flagging an already-satisfied limb.

The advisory changed-character ratio (0.701) is justified here: removing at-will revocation necessarily requires inserting a revocation standard, and the added sentence is confined to that purpose; the balance of the paragraph (copying/reverse-engineering restrictions) is preserved verbatim.

Comment is concise, in first person plural, states what changed and why, and offers the fallback (affiliate coverage on written notice). Minor, non-blocking point: 'Affiliates' and 'Subcontractors acting on Customer's behalf' may not be defined terms for the Customer side in this agreement, so a definitional hook or lowercase usage could be confirmed at drafting.
